subject: Orca Analytics — dedicated GPU pool coordination and allocation
messages:
From: Kevin Li <kevin.li@orca-analytics.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: gina.morales@orca-analytics.com, procurement@orca-analytics.com
Date: 2026-12-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated pool ask for upcoming enterprise deployment

Hi Jonas / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Orca's engineering and ML teams are ready to move into a staged enterprise deployment. Before we commit to a term, we need a dedicated GPU pool (NVIDIA A10x or equivalent) with the following baseline: 20 GPUs reserved, ability to burst to 30 GPUs for sustained 4-hour windows during training runs, and autoscaling to handle peak inference traffic (expected 75 req/s, median seq len 512).

We've attached a short worksheet with projected throughput and preferred contract term (orca_capacity_request.xlsx). Key asks:
- Baseline reservation for Q1 (12-month commitment preferred)
- An autoscaling exception to allow burst to 150% of baseline without pre-warming locks
- A SLA note about fallback behavior if burst capacity is unavailable

Can you confirm feasibility and likely lead time to provision a dedicated pool? If helpful, procurement@orca-analytics.com is cc'd for commercial coordination.

Best,
Kevin Li
Head of Platform, Orca Analytics
kevin.li@orca-analytics.com

- Ops: what changes to autoscale policy would we need and any risk to other customers?
- Commercial: do we want to tie burst guarantees to term length (e.g., 12-mo reservation for burst SLA)?

Please reply with a short plan and blockers. I can join a sync with Kevin if useful.

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-05T13:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated pool ask for upcoming enterprise deployment

Quick feasibility note from infra:
- Carving a 20-GPU baseline out of our US-dedicated cluster is doable within 3-5 business days provided current reservations don't change. To support burst to 30 GPUs, we have two options:
  1) Provision a reserved burst slab (hot spare pool) tagged for Orca — adds lead time but clean isolation.
  2) Grant an autoscaling policy exception to allow their pool to temporarily borrow capacity from the shared burst pool up to 150%. This is faster but increases risk during wide cluster pressure.

Technical impacts to call out:
- Option 2 requires temporarily relaxing strict per-tenant soft caps and removing pre-warm lock for the 4-hour windows; we need a canary policy so that if latency SLOs for other tenants degrade beyond threshold X, we automatically throttle Orca's burst.
- We should also enable KV prefix caching for their request patterns to reduce token compute.

Lead times:
- Option 2 (autoscale exception): 48-72 hours to implement policy + monitoring hooks.
- Option 1 (reserved burst slab): 5-7 business days to provision and validate.

I recommend Option 2 as a near-term solution combined with a plan to move them to Option 1 if utilization proves steady. I'll attach a brief runbook and monitoring checks.

Dev Patel
Infrastructure Engineer, Serving Runtime
dev_patel@redwood.ai
Attachment: proposed_allocation_plan.csv

----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-05T15:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated pool ask for upcoming enterprise deployment

Commercial note:
- Deal is currently estimated at $420k ARR for a 12-month reservation (base + burst add-on). If we require a reserved burst slab (Option 1), we should ask for a higher minimum commitment or a one-time provisioning fee to offset fragmentation of the pool.
- If we go Option 2 (autoscale exception), we can offer a smaller reservation discount and a short-term SLA addendum that references the canary throttle. That reduces lead time and keeps price competitive.

Requesting the following confirmations before I talk to procurement:
1) Which option infra prefers (Dev: call between Option 1 vs 2).
2) Expected calendar date when capacity can be guaranteed.
3) Any measurable SLO caveats we should include in the term sheet (e.g., \"burst best-effort with auto-throttle when cluster utilization > 85%\").

I can draft a commercial term sheet and share with procurement once we lock the technical approach.

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Attachment: commercial_term_sheet_v1.pdf

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-12-06T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated pool ask for upcoming enterprise deployment

Ops/playbook perspective:
- I agree with Dev that Option 2 (autoscale exception) is the fastest path to start. I'll own the rollout steps and monitoring:
  * Create a canary rule that watches end-to-end p99 latency and error rate for the shared cluster.
  * Implement a token-based throttle for Orca that triggers at cluster-util > 85%.
  * Add an alert channel (ops-oncall + account manager) for any throttles.

Timeline:
- Policy + monitoring hooks: up in 48 hours (EOD 2026-12-07).
- Production validation window: 72 hours after rollout.
- If steady >70% baseline for 2 weeks, schedule slab reservation conversion (Option 1) to be completed in the following sprint.

I'll prepare the allocation runbook and calendar invites for kickoff. Need confirmation from Sales that Orca will sign 12-month term with the above caveats.

Hannah Schmitt
Operations Lead
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai

- A documented fallback behavior and the canary thresholds you described
- A clear timeline for when we'll be reviewed for a reserved slab if utilization is steady

We are prepared to sign a 12-month reservation and move procurement forward if you can get the policy + monitoring hooks in place by EOD 2026-12-07 and schedule a kickoff call. Please send a calendar invite for a technical kickoff (today/tomorrow).

Attached is the filled worksheet from our infra team.

Best,
Kevin
